slides.title: Money in, money out
slides.slide: L1 Basic · Money in, money out
slides.notes: Name one thing a business owns, one thing it owes and one sale it records. Notes: use a small tuck shop; learners list three items owned (cash, stock, a fridge) and one amount owed to a supplier, then say which is which.

slides.title: Assets, debts and the equation
slides.slide: L2 Awareness · Assets, debts and the equation
slides.notes: Explain that assets equal liabilities plus capital and say why both sides always match. Notes: practice case is assets of 50,000 and liabilities of 20,000, so capital is 30,000; learners change one figure and rebuild the equation.

slides.title: Journal and ledger entries
slides.slide: L3 Foundation · Journal and ledger entries
slides.notes: Record simple transactions as debit and credit entries and balance a ledger account. Notes: post a cash sale of 8,000 and a credit purchase of 3,000 to T-accounts; check total debits equal total credits before moving on.

slides.title: Trial balance and final accounts
slides.slide: L4 Practitioner · Trial balance and final accounts
slides.notes: Prepare a trial balance and a simple income statement from ledger balances. Notes: sales 90,000, cost of goods sold 55,000 and expenses 20,000 give gross profit 35,000 and net profit 15,000; learners find one deliberate slip.

slides.title: Adjustments and ratios
slides.notes: Apply depreciation and accruals, then calculate and interpret profitability ratios. Notes: a machine costing 60,000 at 10 per cent straight line loses 6,000 a year; gross margin of 35,000 on 90,000 sales is 38.9 per cent, so ask what moved it.

slides.title: Group accounts and goodwill
slides.slide: L6 Advanced · Group accounts and goodwill
slides.notes: Prepare a consolidation adjustment and explain goodwill and non-controlling interest. Notes: a parent pays 420,000 for 80 per cent of a company with net assets of 450,000; goodwill is 60,000 and the non-controlling interest is 90,000; learners show the working.

slides.title: Expected credit loss and audit risk
slides.slide: L7 Super expert · Expected credit loss and audit risk
slides.notes: Evaluate an impairment estimate and design audit tests around its judgements. Notes: receivables ageing of 150,000 at 1 per cent, 40,000 at 5 per cent and 10,000 at 30 per cent gives an allowance of 6,500; challenge each rate with past write-off data.
